title: Global Reallocation of Capital in the Era of Geo-Economic Fragmentation and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: arXiv:2609.18976v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper studies how geo-economic fragmentation affects the international allocation of capital in an economy where artificial intelligence (AI) relies on specialized, mobile investment. We develop a heterogeneous-agent open-economy model with AI-specific capital and geopolitical frictions in cross-border asset holdings. These frictions reduce capital mobility, raise the cost of AI adoption, and generate distributional effects across countries and households. The quantitative results show that fragmentation produces welfare losses that rise nonlinearly with geopolitical distance. These losses are larger for AI-lagging economies and for low-wealth households, mainly through reduced investment, weaker labor income, and tighter financial conditions. translated_title: 地缘经济碎片化与人工智能时代的全球资本再配置
translated_abstract: 本文研究了在地缘经济碎片化的背景下，当人工智能依赖于专业化、可流动的投资时，碎片化如何影响资本的国际配置。我们构建了一个包含AI专用资本以及跨境资产持有中地缘政治摩擦的异质性主体开放经济模型。这些摩擦降低了资本流动性，提高了AI应用的成本，并在国家与家庭之间产生了分配效应。定量结果表明，碎片化造成的福利损失随地缘政治距离呈非线性上升。对于AI落后经济体和低财富家庭而言，这些损失更大，其传导渠道主要是投资减少、劳动收入下降和金融条件收紧。本文还定义了所谓的“碎片化-AI三难困境”：经济体无法同时保持货币自主权、维持高效的AI资本配置，并使自己免受地缘政治碎片化的影响。
tldr: 本文构建了包含AI专用资本与地缘政治摩擦的异质性主体开放经济模型，发现地缘经济碎片化导致随地缘政治距离非线性上升的福利损失，对AI落后经济体和低财富家庭伤害最大，并提出经济体无法兼顾货币自主、高效AI资本配置与地缘政治绝缘的“碎片化-AI三难困境”。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a heterogeneous-agent open-economy model with AI-specific capital and geopolitical frictions, showing that geo-economic fragmentation causes welfare losses rising nonlinearly with geopolitical distance—harming AI-lagging economies and low-wealth households most—and introduces the "Fragmented-AI Trilemma."
